⚠ EMERGENCY: Chest pain or difficulty breathing can be life-threatening.

STOP all activity. Sit or lie down.
Do NOT eat or drink anything.
Call 108 (Ambulance) immediately.

If you have aspirin and no allergy, chew one tablet while waiting for help.

You may have a fever.

• Rest and stay in a cool room
• Drink plenty of water or ORS
• Take an over-the-counter fever medicine (e.g. paracetamol)
• Monitor temperature every 2–3 hours

See a doctor if fever exceeds 40°C or lasts more than 3 days.

For a headache:

• Rest in a quiet, dark room
• Drink water — dehydration is a common cause
• Apply a cool cloth to your forehead
• Take an over-the-counter pain reliever

Seek emergency care if the headache is sudden and very severe, or comes with vision changes or stiff neck.

Sounds like a common cold.

• Rest well
• Drink warm fluids (honey-ginger tea, warm water with lemon)
• Gargle with warm salt water for throat pain
• Avoid cold drinks and spicy food

Consult a doctor if symptoms last more than 7–10 days or fever develops.

For digestive problems:

• Drink ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution) or clean water frequently
• Eat bland foods: rice, banana, plain toast
• Avoid dairy, spicy, and fatty food
• Rest

Seek medical help if symptoms persist beyond 2 days, or if you see blood.

⚠ EMERGENCY: Someone is unconscious or having a seizure.

1. Call 108 immediately
2. Place them on their side (recovery position)
3. Do NOT put anything in their mouth
4. Do NOT leave them alone
5. Stay on the line with emergency services
